rv.q: It isn't original and it certainly isn't politically correct but it's still a glittering, occasionally gobsmacking night out.
So Impossible is not a brave new dawn for British magic.
Impossible cannot reinvent the genre and knows it. It can only put new spins on old tricks.

It has been over a hundred years since the famous magician Henry Houdini performed one of his great escape acts in front of over 4000 people at London’s Hippodrome. This summer the production of Impossible at the Noel Coward Theatre brings back magic to the capital with its attempt to give It a fresh and a contemporary twist.

cn.t: A flashy magic spectacle packing in every traditional illusion imaginable, from vanishing cars to death-defying escapes. Critics find it occasionally spectacular but unoriginal and uneven—glittering fun, though not essential viewing.
